translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: etwas mit einem Luftzug forttragen, umlagern

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see blow, away.
To cause to go away by blowing, or by wind.

examples.text: He blew away the dust which had collected on the book.

Perhaps as startling as the sheer toll was the devastation to some of the state’s well-known locales. Boardwalks along the beach in Seaside Heights, Belmar and other towns on the Jersey Shore were blown away. Amusement parks, arcades and restaurants all but vanished. Bridges to barrier islands buckled, preventing residents from even inspecting the damage to their property.

glosses: To disperse or to depart on currents of air.

examples.text: I didn't have to rake. The leaves just blew away.

glosses: To kill (someone) by shooting them with a firearm.

examples.text: The kid just blew the clerk away.

glosses: To utterly destroy, especially with overwhelming force.

examples.text: In the end, the question proved to be academic. When SCP-3125 arrived, whether it knew ω-0 was there or not, it took no special action against it, and had no need to. Most of ω-0's members' anchors were Foundationers, or Foundation-adjacent. With those people's minds blown away in the first strike, the dense web of mutual memory which had held the Task Force together since its formation tore loose. More than half of the Task Force was cast into the void and died; the final, real death they had evaded for years.

glosses: To flabbergast; to impress greatly.

examples.text: The critics were blown away by their latest album.

glosses: To overwhelm.

examples.text: Newcastle were completely blown away during the opening half of the match but worked up a head of steam after the interval that saw them score four goals in 19 minutes against a bruised and beleaguered Arsenal.

glosses: To cause to go away; to get rid of.

examples.text: And when skipper Richie McCaw hoisted the Webb Ellis Trophy high into the night, a quarter of a century of hurt was blown away in an explosion of fireworks and cheering.

glosses: To delete (data, files, etc.).

glosses: разнести, унести в разные стороны; раздуть (ветром, дуновением ветра)

examples.text: Вороха́ колосьев я подгребал к крестцам, чтобы не развеяло ветром.

glosses: заставить разнестись по ветру, распространиться в воздухе

examples.text: Кости их истребил огонь, пепел развеял ветер…

glosses: перен. заставить рассеяться, исчезнуть

examples.text: Дыхание у́тра легко развеяло сумрачную серую тьму ночи…
Совсем рассвело, наступил короткий осенний день и сырой ветер развеял туман.

glosses: перен. рассеять, уничтожить

examples.text: Однако этот разговор не только не развеял его сомнений относительно славянских племён, но, наоборот, насторожил.

glosses: заставить колыхаться, колебаться в воздухе, на ветру

examples.text: Паруса развейте в воздухе, // Дерзко правьте корабли!
